    def scenario_to_world(x: float, y: float, z: float = 0.0) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Default embedding of the right-handed scenario frame in the left-handed world.

    Flips ``y``. Used by the synthetic helpers; the CARLA runtime places
    scenarios with its own site transform. A scenario heading ``h`` (radians)
    becomes the world yaw ``-degrees(h)``.
    """
    return float(x), float(-y), float(z)

    def synthetic_agents(scenario: Mapping[str, Any], t: float,
                     ground_z: float = 0.0) -> List[AgentState]:
    """Scripted agents at time ``t`` with testbench box sizes.

    Positions are placed with :func:`scenario_to_world`; speeds are in m/s.
    """
    tb = _testbench()
    agents: List[AgentState] = []
    for agent_def in scenario["agents"]:
        pose = tb.interpolate_agent(agent_def, t)
        if pose is None:
            continue
        obj = tb.OBJECT_TYPES[KIND_TO_OBJECT.get(agent_def["type"], "pedestrian")]
        agents.append(AgentState(
            id=int(agent_def["id"]), kind=agent_def["type"], sx=float(pose["x"]),
            sy=float(pose["y"]), heading=float(pose["heading"]),
            speed=float(tb.estimate_agent_speed(agent_def, t)),
            location=scenario_to_world(pose["x"], pose["y"], ground_z + obj.height / 2.0),
            rotation=(0.0, -math.degrees(pose["heading"]), 0.0),
            extent=(obj.length / 2.0, obj.width / 2.0, obj.height / 2.0),
            model=str(agent_def.get("model", "")),
        ))
    return agents

    def synthetic_frame(scenario: Mapping[str, Any], index: int, fps: int,
                    cameras: Optional[Dict[str, CameraModel]] = None,
                    states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> FrameRecord:
    """A :class:`FrameRecord` at ``t = index / fps`` built from the scenario alone, without images.

    ``state`` is ``states[index]`` when given, else ``"idle"``; in the alert
    state ``alert_pair`` is the closest bike and pedestrian.
    """
    t = index / float(fps)
    state = states[index] if states is not None and index < len(states) else "idle"
    frame = FrameRecord(index=index, t=t, agents=synthetic_agents(scenario, t), state=state,
                        states={"default": state}, danger=danger_record(scenario, t),
                        cameras=dict(cameras or {}))
    if state == "alert":
        pair = closest_pair(frame)
        if pair is not None:
            frame.alert_pair = (pair[0], pair[1])
    return frame

    def frame_ground_truth(frame: FrameRecord, view: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Per-agent ground truth of one view, JSON-safe.

    Each entry has ``id``, ``kind``, ``role``, ``bbox`` (pixels, clipped to
    the image), ``corners_image`` (8 ``[u, v]`` or ``None``), ``distance_m``,
    ``truncation`` and ``visible_fraction``. The visible fraction is the share
    of the agent's projected silhouette carrying its id in
    ``aux['<view>/instance']`` when that buffer and ``AgentState.instance_id``
    exist, else the share of camera-facing box surface samples not occluded in
    ``aux['<view>/depth']`` (planar depth for pinhole views, range for
    fisheye views), else ``None``. Agents outside the view are omitted.
    """
    from .projection import project_box

    cam = frame.cameras.get(view)
    if cam is None:
        return []
    depth = frame.aux.get(f"{view}/depth")
    instance = frame.aux.get(f"{view}/instance")
    objects: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for agent in frame.agents:
        box = project_box(agent, cam)
        if box is None:
            continue
        visible: Optional[float] = None
        if instance is not None:
            visible = _visible_from_instance(agent, cam, instance)
        if visible is None and depth is not None:
            visible = _visible_from_depth(agent, cam, depth)
        corners = [None if not np.all(np.isfinite(c)) else [round(float(c[0]), 2),
                                                             round(float(c[1]), 2)]
                   for c in box["corners_image"]]
        objects.append({
            "id": agent.id, "kind": agent.kind, "role": agent.role,
            "bbox": [round(float(v), 2) for v in box["bbox"]],
            "corners_image": corners,
            "distance_m": round(float(box["distance_m"]), 3),
            "truncation": round(float(box["truncation"]), 4),
            "visible_fraction": None if visible is None else round(visible, 4),
        })
    return objects

    overlay ¶

    HUD overlay and schematic top-down panel for rendered scenario frames.

    draw_overlay annotates one camera view with 3D boxes, id chips, ground trails, the bike-pedestrian connector, the decision state badge and a timeline of ground-truth danger against the system's alerts. draw_bev renders the same frame as a plan view in the scenario frame. Both work on BGR uint8 arrays, return new arrays and scale every size with the image height, so 720p and 4K output look the same.

    Pixel coordinates follow bikeped.sim.projection: continuous, with pixel i covering [i, i + 1).

    Run python -m bikeped.sim.overlay --demo OUT_DIR to render a still and a short clip over a synthetic backdrop without a simulator.

    def build_timeline(scenario: Dict[str, Any], fps: int,
                   states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Precompute what the timeline strip shows for one scenario.

    Frame ``i`` is at ``t = i / fps``. Ground-truth danger comes from
    ``decision_testbench.compute_ground_truth_danger``. ``states`` is the
    decision state per frame as recorded by a run; when it is ``None`` the
    states come from ``decision_testbench.simulate_scenario`` with the default
    pipeline configuration and no detection noise, and the result is cached
    per scenario and frame rate.

    Returns a dict with ``duration`` (s), ``fps``, ``n`` (frames), ``states``,
    the interval lists ``danger``, ``actionable``, ``alert`` and ``warning``
    (``[t0, t1]`` pairs in seconds, ``t1`` exclusive), and ``first_alert_t``
    and ``first_danger_t`` (seconds or ``None``).
    """
    tb = _testbench()
    fps = int(fps)
    key = (_scenario_key(scenario), fps)
    if states is None and key in _TIMELINES:
        return _TIMELINES[key]
    dt = 1.0 / fps
    duration = float(tb.get_scenario_duration(scenario))
    if states is None:
        result = tb.simulate_scenario(scenario, tb.PIPELINE_CONFIGS["default"], fps=fps)
        state_list = [str(s) for s in result["states"]]
        danger = [bool(d) for d in result["dangers"]]
        actionable = [bool(a.actionable) for a in result["assessments"]]
        _DANGER[(key[0], fps, len(state_list))] = (danger, actionable)
    else:
        state_list = [str(s) for s in states]
        cached = _DANGER.get((key[0], fps, len(state_list)))
        if cached is None:
            assessments = [tb.compute_ground_truth_danger(scenario, i * dt)
                           for i in range(len(state_list))]
            cached = ([bool(a.is_danger) for a in assessments],
                      [bool(a.actionable) for a in assessments])
            _DANGER[(key[0], fps, len(state_list))] = cached
        danger, actionable = cached
    n = len(state_list)
    alert = [s == "alert" for s in state_list]
    timeline = {
        "duration": max(duration, n * dt),
        "fps": fps,
        "n": n,
        "states": state_list,
        "danger": _intervals(danger, dt),
        "actionable": _intervals(actionable, dt),
        "alert": _intervals(alert, dt),
        "warning": _intervals([s == "warning" for s in state_list], dt),
        "first_alert_t": round(alert.index(True) * dt, 4) if any(alert) else None,
        "first_danger_t": round(danger.index(True) * dt, 4) if any(danger) else None,
    }
    if states is None:
        _TIMELINES[key] = timeline
    return timeline

    def draw_overlay(image: np.ndarray, frame: FrameRecord, view: str, *, run: RunInfo,
                 scenario: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
                 style: Optional[OverlayStyle] = None,
                 history: Optional[Sequence[FrameRecord]] = None,
                 timeline: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Draw the HUD over one rendered view and return the annotated copy.

    ``image`` is the BGR ``uint8`` frame of ``view`` and is not modified. The
    camera model is ``frame.cameras[view]``; without one only the screen-space
    elements (badge, caption, timeline) are drawn. ``history`` holds earlier
    frames, oldest first, and feeds the ground trails from the bottom centre of
    each agent's box in the world frame. ``timeline`` is the result of
    ``build_timeline``; when it is ``None`` and ``scenario`` is given it is
    built from the scenario at ``run.fps``.
    """
    style = style or DEFAULT_STYLE
    out = np.ascontiguousarray(image).copy()
    if out.ndim == 2:
        out = cv2.cvtColor(out, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR)
    canvas = _Canvas(out, style)
    cam = frame.cameras.get(view)
    if timeline is None and scenario is not None and style.timeline:
        timeline = build_timeline(scenario, run.fps)
    show_timeline = style.timeline and timeline is not None

    margin = canvas.px(28)
    lanes_h = 2 * canvas.px(6, 3) + canvas.px(5, 2)
    timeline_y = canvas.h - margin - lanes_h
    caption_font = canvas.px(16, 9)
    caption_h = canvas.text_size("Ag", caption_font)[1]
    caption_y = (timeline_y - canvas.px(14) - caption_h) if show_timeline else (
        canvas.h - margin - caption_h)
    hud_top = caption_y if style.caption else (timeline_y if show_timeline else canvas.h)
    if style.caption or show_timeline:
        canvas.scrim(int(hud_top - canvas.px(70)), canvas.h, 0.0, 0.66)

    occupied: List[Rect] = []
    if style.caption or show_timeline:
        occupied.append((0.0, hud_top - canvas.px(6), float(canvas.w), float(canvas.h)))
    badge_h = canvas.px(42, 20)
    if style.badge:
        occupied.append((0.0, 0.0, margin + canvas.px(250), margin + badge_h + canvas.px(40)))

    scripted = [a for a in frame.agents if a.role == "scripted"]
    if cam is not None:
        ground_z = run.site.get("ground_z")
        if ground_z is None:
            ground_z = min((_bottom_center(a)[2] for a in frame.agents), default=0.0)
        if style.rings or view in style.ring_views:
            boxes = [project_box(a, cam) for a in frame.agents]
            _draw_rings(canvas, cam, float(ground_z), occupied,
                        [tuple(b["bbox"]) for b in boxes if b is not None])
        if style.trails and history:
            _draw_trails(canvas, frame, cam, history)

        pair = _pair(frame) if style.connector else None
        highlighted = set()
        if pair is not None and pair[2] <= style.connector_max_m:
            a, b, distance = pair
            color = _connector_color(style, frame.state)
            if frame.state in ("alert", "warning"):
                highlighted = {a.id, b.id}
            ends = np.stack([_bottom_center(a), _bottom_center(b)])
            pieces = project_polyline(ends, cam)
            canvas.lines(pieces, style.bgr("background"), canvas.px(5), alpha=0.45)
            canvas.lines(pieces, color, canvas.px(2))
            uv, valid, _ = project_points(ends.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True), cam)
            if valid[0] and 0 <= uv[0, 0] < canvas.w and 0 <= uv[0, 1] < canvas.h:
                label = f"{distance:.1f} m"
                font = canvas.px(15, 9)
                tw, th = canvas.text_size(label, font, bold=True)
                pad = canvas.px(9)
                rect = (uv[0, 0] - tw / 2.0 - pad, uv[0, 1] - th / 2.0 - canvas.px(4),
                        uv[0, 0] + tw / 2.0 + pad, uv[0, 1] + th / 2.0 + canvas.px(4))
                canvas.plate(rect, style.bgr("background"), alpha=0.86)
                canvas.text_centered(rect, label, font, color, bold=True)
                occupied.append(rect)

        cam_pos = np.asarray(cam.position, dtype=np.float64)
        ordered = sorted(frame.agents, reverse=True,
                         key=lambda ag: float(np.linalg.norm(np.asarray(ag.location) - cam_pos)))
        chips: List[Tuple[AgentState, Sequence[float]]] = []
        for agent in ordered:
            color = style.agent_color(agent.kind, agent.role)
            hot = agent.id in highlighted and agent.role == "scripted"
            if style.boxes:
                _draw_box(canvas, agent, cam, color,
                          style.state_color(frame.state) if hot else color, 0.34 if hot else 0.2)
            if style.labels and agent.role == "scripted":
                box = project_box(agent, cam)
                if box is not None:
                    chips.append((agent, box["bbox"]))
        font = canvas.px(14, 9)
        for agent, bbox in reversed(chips):
            text = _chip_text(agent)
            tw, _ = canvas.text_size(text, font, bold=True)
            size = (tw + 2 * canvas.px(8), canvas.px(22, 13))
            rect = _place_chip(canvas, size, bbox, occupied)
            occupied.append(rect)
            color = style.agent_color(agent.kind)
            anchor = ((bbox[0] + bbox[2]) / 2.0, bbox[1])
            foot = ((rect[0] + rect[2]) / 2.0, rect[3])
            if math.hypot(anchor[0] - foot[0], anchor[1] - foot[1]) > canvas.px(10):
                canvas.lines([np.array([foot, anchor])], color, canvas.px(1.25), alpha=0.6)
            outline = style.state_color(frame.state) if agent.id in highlighted else None
            _draw_chip(canvas, rect, text, color, outline)

    if style.badge:
        canvas.scrim(0, margin + badge_h + canvas.px(50), 0.3, 0.0)
        badge = _draw_badge(canvas, margin, margin, frame.state)
        danger = frame.danger or {}
        if danger.get("is_danger"):
            sep = " \u00b7 " if canvas.fonts.truetype else " | "
            note = "Ground truth: danger"
            if danger.get("ttc") is not None and math.isfinite(float(danger["ttc"])):
                note += f"{sep}TTC {float(danger['ttc']):.1f} s"
            font = canvas.px(13, 9)
            tw, th = canvas.text_size(note, font)
            pad = canvas.px(12)
            top = badge[3] + canvas.px(8)
            rect = (margin, top, margin + tw + 2 * pad, top + th + canvas.px(10))
            canvas.plate(rect, style.bgr("background"), alpha=0.7)
            canvas.text_centered(rect, note, font, style.bgr("alert"))

    if style.caption:
        sep = "  \u00b7  " if canvas.fonts.truetype else "  |  "
        title, details = _caption_parts(frame, run, sep)
        tw, _ = canvas.text(margin, caption_y, title, caption_font, style.bgr("text"), bold=True)
        if details:
            canvas.text(margin + tw, caption_y, sep + details, caption_font, style.bgr("muted"))
        total = timeline["duration"] if timeline else run.duration_s
        clock = f"{frame.t:5.2f} s" + (f" / {total:.2f} s" if total else "")
        cw, _ = canvas.text_size(clock, caption_font)
        canvas.text(canvas.w - margin - cw, caption_y, clock, caption_font, style.bgr("text"))
        tag = view.upper()
        vw, _ = canvas.text_size(tag, canvas.px(12, 8), bold=True)
        canvas.text(canvas.w - margin - cw - canvas.px(18) - vw,
                    caption_y + (caption_h - canvas.text_size(tag, canvas.px(12, 8), True)[1]) / 2,
                    tag, canvas.px(12, 8), style.bgr("muted"), bold=True)
    if show_timeline:
        _draw_timeline(canvas, timeline, frame.t, margin, canvas.w - margin, timeline_y)
    if scripted and cam is None:
        _LOG.debug("view %s has no camera model; drew screen-space HUD only", view)
    return out

    def draw_bev(frame: FrameRecord, *, run: RunInfo, scenario: Optional[Dict[str, Any]],
             size: Tuple[int, int] = (1080, 1080), style: Optional[OverlayStyle] = None,
             history: Optional[Sequence[FrameRecord]] = None,
             timeline: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Render the frame as a schematic plan view in the scenario frame.

    ``size`` is ``(width, height)`` in pixels. The panel shows the road, the
    crosswalk at ``x = 5``, the camera marker at ``run.site['camera_xy']``
    (the testbench camera position when absent) with the proximity rings of
    the default pipeline, the scripted paths, and every agent as an oriented
    glyph with a short trail. Scenario ``x`` points right and ``y`` up. Trails
    come from the scenario paths when ``scenario`` is given and from
    ``history`` otherwise. ``timeline`` adds the timeline strip at the bottom.
    """
    style = style or DEFAULT_STYLE
    width, height = int(size[0]), int(size[1])
    cam_xy = _camera_xy(run)
    window = _bev_window(scenario, frame, cam_xy)
    key = (width, height, style, _scenario_key(scenario) if scenario else None,
           tuple(round(v, 3) for v in window), cam_xy)
    static = _BEV_STATIC.get(key)
    if static is None:
        static = _BEV_STATIC[key] = _bev_static((width, height), style, scenario, window, cam_xy)
        if len(_BEV_STATIC) > 8:
            _BEV_STATIC.popitem(last=False)
    out = static.copy()
    canvas = _Canvas(out, style)
    canvas.s = style.scale * min(width, height) / 1080.0
    to_px = _bev_mapper((width, height), window)
    metre = float(to_px([[1.0, 0.0]])[0][0] - to_px([[0.0, 0.0]])[0][0])
    bg = style.bgr("background")

    pair = _pair(frame) if style.connector else None
    highlighted = set()
    if pair is not None and pair[2] <= style.connector_max_m:
        a, b, distance = pair
        color = _connector_color(style, frame.state)
        if frame.state in ("alert", "warning"):
            highlighted = {a.id, b.id}
        ends = to_px([[a.sx, a.sy], [b.sx, b.sy]])
        canvas.lines([ends], color, canvas.px(2), alpha=0.9)
        mid = ends.mean(axis=0)
        label = f"{distance:.1f} m"
        font = canvas.px(15, 9)
        tw, th = canvas.text_size(label, font, bold=True)
        normal = np.array([-(ends[1][1] - ends[0][1]), ends[1][0] - ends[0][0]])
        length = float(np.linalg.norm(normal))
        if length > 1e-6:
            normal = normal / length
            if normal[1] > 0:
                normal = -normal
            mid = mid + normal * (th / 2.0 + canvas.px(12))
        rect = (mid[0] - tw / 2.0 - canvas.px(9), mid[1] - th / 2.0 - canvas.px(4),
                mid[0] + tw / 2.0 + canvas.px(9), mid[1] + th / 2.0 + canvas.px(4))
        canvas.plate(rect, bg, alpha=0.9)
        canvas.text_centered(rect, label, font, color, bold=True)

    for agent in frame.agents:
        color = style.agent_color(agent.kind, agent.role)
        if style.trails and agent.role == "scripted":
            trail = to_px(_bev_trail(frame, agent, scenario, history, style.trail_seconds))
            edges = np.linspace(0, len(trail) - 1, 6).round().astype(int)
            for band in range(5):
                chunk = trail[edges[band]:edges[band + 1] + 1]
                canvas.lines([chunk], color, canvas.px(4), alpha=0.18 + 0.62 * (band + 1) / 5)

    font = canvas.px(14, 9)
    for agent in frame.agents:
        color = style.agent_color(agent.kind, agent.role)
        center = to_px([[agent.sx, agent.sy]])[0]
        direction = np.array([math.cos(agent.heading), -math.sin(agent.heading)])
        side = np.array([-direction[1], direction[0]])
        if agent.kind == "person":
            radius = max(canvas.px(8), 0.3 * metre)
            reach = radius
            if agent.id in highlighted:
                canvas.circle((center[0], center[1]), radius * 2.1,
                              style.state_color(frame.state), thickness=canvas.px(2))
            canvas.circle((center[0], center[1]), radius + canvas.px(2), bg)
            canvas.circle((center[0], center[1]), radius, color)
            if agent.speed > 0.05:
                tip = center + direction * radius * 1.9
                canvas.lines([np.stack([center + direction * radius, tip])], color, canvas.px(3))
        else:
            length = max(canvas.px(30), 2.0 * agent.extent[0] * metre)
            half_w = max(canvas.px(7), agent.extent[1] * metre)
            reach = length / 2.0
            glyph = np.stack([center + direction * length / 2.0,
                              center - direction * length / 2.0 + side * half_w,
                              center - direction * length / 4.0,
                              center - direction * length / 2.0 - side * half_w])
            if agent.id in highlighted:
                canvas.circle((center[0], center[1]), length * 0.78,
                              style.state_color(frame.state), thickness=canvas.px(2))
            canvas.lines([glyph], bg, canvas.px(5), closed=True)
            canvas.polygon(glyph, color)
        if style.labels and agent.role == "scripted":
            text = _chip_text(agent)
            tw, _ = canvas.text_size(text, font, bold=True)
            cw, ch = tw + 2 * canvas.px(8), canvas.px(22, 13)
            x = center[0] + reach * 0.75 + canvas.px(8)
            y = center[1] - reach * 0.75 - canvas.px(8) - ch
            x = min(max(x, canvas.px(6)), width - cw - canvas.px(6))
            y = min(max(y, canvas.px(6)), height - ch - canvas.px(6))
            _draw_chip(canvas, (x, y, x + cw, y + ch), text, color)

    pad = canvas.px(28)
    if style.badge:
        _draw_badge(canvas, width - pad, pad, frame.state, align_right=True)
    if timeline is not None and style.timeline:
        lanes_h = 2 * canvas.px(6, 3) + canvas.px(5, 2)
        bar = float(to_px([[5.0, 0.0]])[0][0] - to_px([[0.0, 0.0]])[0][0])
        _draw_timeline(canvas, timeline, frame.t, pad, width - pad - bar - canvas.px(28),
                       height - pad - lanes_h)
    return out

    def render_demo(out_dir: Any, scenario_id: str = "Bike Approaches Ped", fps: int = 30,
                size: Tuple[int, int] = (1920, 1080)) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Render the HUD and the plan view for one scenario without a simulator.

    A pole-height pinhole camera at the testbench camera position looks at the
    crosswalk over an analytic street backdrop, with agents placed from the
    scenario paths. Writes ``demo_view.png`` (the camera view with the HUD),
    ``demo_bev.png``, ``demo_still.png`` (split layout), ``demo_fisheye.png``
    when the fisheye module is available, and ``demo.mp4``. Returns the paths
    under ``files`` together with the timeline of the scenario.
    """
    from .groundtruth import scenario_to_world, synthetic_frame

    out = Path(out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    scenario = _find_scenario(scenario_id)
    timeline = build_timeline(scenario, fps)
    width, height = int(size[0]), int(size[1])
    ref = _testbench().FisheyeCamera()
    position = scenario_to_world(ref.cam_x, ref.cam_y, ref.height)
    target = scenario_to_world(_CROSSWALK_X_M + 3.0, 0.0, 0.6)
    pole = _look_at("pole", position, target, width, height, fov_deg=90.0)
    cameras = {"pole": pole}
    run = RunInfo(scenario_name=scenario["name"],
                  scenario_id=str(scenario.get("id", scenario["name"].lower().replace(" ", "-"))),
                  fps=fps, duration_s=timeline["duration"], engine="synthetic",
                  weather="clear_noon", views=["pole"],
                  site={"camera_xy": (ref.cam_x, ref.cam_y), "ground_z": 0.0})
    backdrop = _synthetic_backdrop(pole)
    style = DEFAULT_STYLE
    bev_side = min(height, 1080)

    from .compose import compose, fit_size

    out_size = fit_size("split", (width, height), height)

    def render(index: int, frames: List[FrameRecord]) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        frame = frames[index]
        base = backdrop.copy()
        _paint_stand_ins(base, frame, pole)
        history = frames[max(0, index - int(style.trail_seconds * fps)):index]
        view = draw_overlay(base, frame, "pole", run=run, scenario=scenario, style=style,
                            history=history, timeline=timeline)
        bev = draw_bev(frame, run=run, scenario=scenario, size=(bev_side, bev_side), style=style)
        composite = compose("split", [view], bev, size=out_size)
        return view, bev, composite

    frames = [synthetic_frame(scenario, i, fps, cameras=cameras, states=timeline["states"])
              for i in range(timeline["n"])]
    alerts = timeline["alert"]
    if alerts:
        start, end = max(alerts, key=lambda iv: iv[1] - iv[0])
        still_index = int(round((start + 0.55 * (end - start)) * fps))
    else:
        still_index = timeline["n"] // 2
    still_index = min(max(still_index, 0), timeline["n"] - 1)
    view, bev, composite = render(still_index, frames)
    files = {"view": out / "demo_view.png", "bev": out / "demo_bev.png",
             "still": out / "demo_still.png", "clip": out / "demo.mp4"}
    cv2.imwrite(str(files["view"]), view)
    cv2.imwrite(str(files["bev"]), bev)
    cv2.imwrite(str(files["still"]), composite)

    try:
        from .fisheye import FisheyeRemap, deployed_fisheye_model

        model = deployed_fisheye_model(position, -90.0, scale=0.5)
        remap = FisheyeRemap(model, face_size=768)
        frame = replace(frames[still_index], cameras={"fisheye": model})
        faces = {}
        for face in remap.faces:
            face_cam = remap.face_camera(face)
            faces[face] = _synthetic_backdrop(face_cam, supersample=1)
            _paint_stand_ins(faces[face], frame, face_cam)
        fisheye = remap.remap(faces)
        files["fisheye"] = out / "demo_fisheye.png"
        cv2.imwrite(str(files["fisheye"]), draw_overlay(
            fisheye, frame, "fisheye", run=run, scenario=scenario, style=style,
            history=frames[max(0, still_index - int(style.trail_seconds * fps)):still_index],
            timeline=timeline))
    except ImportError:
        _LOG.info("fisheye module not available; skipping the fisheye still")

    from .recorder import VideoSink

    writer = VideoSink(files["clip"], fps)
    try:
        for index in range(timeline["n"]):
            writer.write(render(index, frames)[2])
    finally:
        writer.close()
    return {"files": {k: str(v) for k, v in files.items()}, "timeline": timeline,
            "still_index": still_index}

    def main(argv: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> int:
    """Command line entry point: ``python -m bikeped.sim.overlay --demo OUT_DIR``."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="python -m bikeped.sim.overlay",
        description="Render the HUD and plan view over a synthetic backdrop, without a simulator.")
    parser.add_argument("--demo", metavar="OUT_DIR", required=True,
                        help="directory that receives the stills and the clip")
    parser.add_argument("--scenario", default="Bike Approaches Ped",
                        help="scenario name or id (default: %(default)s)")
    parser.add_argument("--fps", type=int, default=30)
    parser.add_argument("--size", default="1920x1080", help="output size as WIDTHxHEIGHT")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    width, height = (int(v) for v in args.size.lower().split("x"))
    result = render_demo(args.demo, args.scenario, fps=args.fps, size=(width, height))
    for path in result["files"].values():
        print(path)
    return 0

    compose ¶

    Layouts that arrange camera views and the top-down panel into one frame.

    All images are BGR uint8 arrays and sizes are (width, height) in pixels. Every layout returns a frame of exactly the requested size, so the composite video keeps one resolution whatever the views look like. Views are never stretched: each one is scaled to fit its cell and centred on the page background.

    letterbox ¶

    letterbox(
    image: ndarray, size: Size, background: Tuple[int, int, int] = BACKGROUND_BGR
) -> np.ndarray

    Fit image inside a frame of size without changing its aspect ratio.

    The image is scaled to the largest size that fits (area averaging when it shrinks, bicubic when it grows), centred, and the rest of the frame is filled with background (BGR). Grayscale and BGRA inputs are converted to BGR.

    def letterbox(
    image: np.ndarray,
    size: Size,
    background: Tuple[int, int, int] = BACKGROUND_BGR,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Fit ``image`` inside a frame of ``size`` without changing its aspect ratio.

    The image is scaled to the largest size that fits (area averaging when it
    shrinks, bicubic when it grows), centred, and the rest of the frame is
    filled with ``background`` (BGR). Grayscale and BGRA inputs are converted
    to BGR.
    """
    width, height = _checked_size(size)
    src = _as_bgr(image)
    src_h, src_w = src.shape[:2]
    scale = min(width / src_w, height / src_h)
    new_w = max(1, min(width, int(round(src_w * scale))))
    new_h = max(1, min(height, int(round(src_h * scale))))
    if (new_w, new_h) != (src_w, src_h):
        interpolation = cv2.INTER_AREA if scale < 1.0 else cv2.INTER_CUBIC
        src = cv2.resize(src, (new_w, new_h), interpolation=interpolation)

    canvas = np.empty((height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
    canvas[:] = background
    x0 = (width - new_w) // 2
    y0 = (height - new_h) // 2
    canvas[y0:y0 + new_h, x0:x0 + new_w] = src
    return canvas

    Frame size at which a view fills its cell of layout without bars.

    view_size is the (width, height) of the camera view, of which only the aspect ratio matters, and height the wanted frame height in pixels. The returned (width, height) is even in both dimensions, as H.264 with 4:2:0 chroma requires.

    def fit_size(layout: str, view_size: Size, height: int = 1080) -> Size:
    """Frame size at which a view fills its cell of ``layout`` without bars.

    ``view_size`` is the ``(width, height)`` of the camera view, of which only
    the aspect ratio matters, and ``height`` the wanted frame height in
    pixels. The returned ``(width, height)`` is even in both dimensions, as
    H.264 with 4:2:0 chroma requires.
    """
    if layout not in LAYOUTS:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown layout {layout!r}; expected one of {', '.join(LAYOUTS)}")
    view_w, view_h = _checked_size(view_size)
    height = _even(int(height))
    aspect = view_w / view_h
    gutter = _gutter(height)
    if layout == "single":
        width = int(round(height * aspect))
    elif layout == "split":
        inner_h = height - 2 * gutter
        width = 3 * gutter + int(round(inner_h * aspect)) + inner_h
    else:
        cell_h = (height - 3 * gutter) // 2
        width = 3 * gutter + 2 * int(round(cell_h * aspect))
    return _even(width), height

    def compose(
    layout: str,
    images: Sequence[np.ndarray],
    bev: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    *,
    size: Size = (1920, 1080),
    labels: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Arrange camera views and the top-down panel into one frame.

    Parameters
    ----------
    layout:
        ``"single"`` shows the first view alone. ``"split"`` puts the first
        view on the left and ``bev`` in a square panel on the right that spans
        the inner height of the frame; without ``bev`` it is the same as
        ``"single"``. ``"quad"`` is a 2x2 grid with up to three views and
        ``bev`` in the last cell; without ``bev`` a fourth view takes that
        cell, and cells with nothing to show stay background.
    images:
        Camera views, primary view first. A single array counts as one view.
    bev:
        Top-down panel, usually from ``overlay.draw_bev``.
    size:
        ``(width, height)`` of the returned frame in pixels.
    labels:
        One short caption per view, drawn in the top-left corner of its cell.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        BGR ``uint8`` frame of shape ``(height, width, 3)``. Margins and
        gutters are 1.5 percent of the frame height and use the page
        background colour.
    """
    if layout not in LAYOUTS:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown layout {layout!r}; expected one of {', '.join(LAYOUTS)}")
    if isinstance(images, np.ndarray) and images.ndim < 4:
        images = [images]
    if images is None or len(images) == 0:
        raise ValueError("compose needs at least one image")
    width, height = _checked_size(size)
    captions = list(labels) if labels is not None else []

    if layout == "single" or (layout == "split" and bev is None):
        frame = letterbox(images[0], (width, height))
        if captions:
            _draw_label(frame, captions[0], (0, 0, width, height))
        return frame

    frame = np.empty((height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
    frame[:] = BACKGROUND_BGR

    if layout == "split":
        view_cell, panel_cell = _split_cells((width, height))
        _place(frame, images[0], view_cell)
        _place(frame, bev, panel_cell)
        if captions:
            _draw_label(frame, captions[0], view_cell)
        return frame

    cells = _quad_cells((width, height))
    view_cells = cells[:3] if bev is not None else cells
    for i, (image, cell) in enumerate(zip(images, view_cells)):
        _place(frame, image, cell)
        if i < len(captions):
            _draw_label(frame, captions[i], cell)
    if bev is not None:
        _place(frame, bev, cells[3])
    return frame

    recorder ¶

    Writes one rendered run to disk: videos, ground truth, stills and the manifest.

    Layout of a run directory (run_id = <engine>_<scenario-id>_<weather>)::

    <out_dir>/<run_id>/
  manifest.json             run metadata, camera models, per-frame records, timeline
  video/<view>.mp4          clean view, H.264
  video/<view>_overlay.mp4  view with the HUD (when overlay is on)
  video/composite.mp4       the chosen layout
  frames/<view>/000000.jpg  only when frames are saved
  gt/<view>.jsonl           one line per frame: 2D boxes, 3D corners, visibility
  stills/                   first frame, first alert, closest bike-pedestrian approach

    Videos are encoded with ffmpeg (libx264, yuv420p) through a pipe; when no ffmpeg executable is found, cv2.VideoWriter with the mp4v codec is used instead and a warning is logged.

    def close(self) -> None:
    """Finish the file. Safe to call more than once."""
    if self._closed:
        return
    self._closed = True
    if self._proc is not None:
        try:
            self._proc.stdin.close()
        except OSError:
            pass
        code = self._proc.wait()
        message = self._ffmpeg_error()
        self._stderr.close()
        if code != 0:
            _LOG.error("ffmpeg exited with %d writing %s: %s", code, self.path, message)
    if self._cv is not None:
        self._cv.release()

    def __init__(self, out_dir: PathLike, run: RunInfo, *, views: Sequence[str],
             overlay: bool = True, layout: str = "single", save_frames: str = "none",
             crf: int = 18, scenario: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
             style: Any = None, composite_height: Optional[int] = None,
             run_id: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    if layout not in LAYOUTS:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown layout {layout!r}; expected one of {LAYOUTS}")
    if save_frames not in SAVE_FRAME_FORMATS:
        raise ValueError(f"save_frames must be one of {SAVE_FRAME_FORMATS}")
    if not views:
        raise ValueError("Recorder needs at least one view")
    self.run = run
    self.views = list(views)
    self.overlay = bool(overlay)
    self.layout = layout
    self.save_frames = save_frames
    self.crf = int(crf)
    self.scenario = scenario
    self.style = style
    self.composite_height = composite_height
    self.run_id = run_id or f"{run.engine}_{run.scenario_id}_{run.weather}"
    self.run_dir = Path(out_dir) / self.run_id
    self.run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    self.fps = float(run.fps or 30)
    self._ffmpeg = find_ffmpeg()
    self._sinks: Dict[str, VideoSink] = {}
    self._gt_files: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    self._cameras: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
    self._records: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    self._history: Deque[FrameRecord] = deque(maxlen=max(2, int(round(1.5 * self.fps)) + 1))
    self._stills: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    self._closest: Optional[float] = None
    self._timeline: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    self._missing: set = set()
    self._closed = False
    self._result: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    self._error: Optional[str] = None

    def write(self, frame: FrameRecord) -> None:
    """Record one frame: videos, ground truth, saved frames, still candidates."""
    if self._closed:
        raise RuntimeError("Recorder is closed")
    shown: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    for view in self.views:
        image = frame.images.get(view)
        if image is None:
            if view not in self._missing:
                _LOG.warning("frame %d has no image for view %r", frame.index, view)
                self._missing.add(view)
            continue
        cam = frame.cameras.get(view)
        if cam is not None and view not in self._cameras:
            self._cameras[view] = cam.to_dict()
        self._sink(view).write(image)
        h, w = image.shape[:2]
        line = {"index": frame.index, "t": round(float(frame.t), 4), "width": w, "height": h,
                "objects": frame_ground_truth(frame, view)}
        self._gt(view).write(json.dumps(_json_safe(line)) + "\n")
        if self.save_frames != "none":
            folder = self.run_dir / "frames" / view
            folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            params = [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, 95] if self.save_frames == "jpg" else []
            cv2.imwrite(str(folder / f"{frame.index:06d}.{self.save_frames}"), image, params)
        if self.overlay:
            annotated = self._draw(image, frame, view)
            self._sink(f"{view}_overlay").write(annotated)
            shown[view] = annotated
        else:
            shown[view] = image
    if shown:
        composite = self._composite(frame, shown)
        self._sink("composite").write(composite)
        self._note_stills(frame, composite)
    self._records.append(frame.to_dict())
    self._history.append(replace(frame, images={}, aux={}))

    def timeline_summary(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Frame counts per state, alert and danger intervals, first alert and lead time.

    ``lead_time_s`` is the onset of the first ground-truth danger interval
    minus the first alert time (positive when the alert came first); it is
    ``None`` unless both exist. Times are seconds of scenario time.
    """
    from .types import STATES

    times = [r["t"] for r in self._records]
    states = [r["state"] for r in self._records]
    danger = [bool((r.get("danger") or {}).get("is_danger")) for r in self._records]
    actionable = [bool((r.get("danger") or {}).get("actionable")) for r in self._records]
    dt = 1.0 / self.fps
    alert = _intervals(times, [s == "alert" for s in states], dt)
    danger_iv = _intervals(times, danger, dt)
    first_alert = alert[0][0] if alert else None
    first_danger = danger_iv[0][0] if danger_iv else None
    closest = None
    best = None
    for r in self._records:
        people = [a for a in r["agents"] if a["kind"] == "person" and a["role"] == "scripted"]
        bikes = [a for a in r["agents"] if a["kind"] == "bike" and a["role"] == "scripted"]
        for b in bikes:
            for p in people:
                d = math.hypot(b["sx"] - p["sx"], b["sy"] - p["sy"])
                if best is None or d < best:
                    best = d
                    closest = {"index": r["index"], "t": r["t"], "bike_id": b["id"],
                               "person_id": p["id"], "distance_m": round(d, 3)}
    return {
        "frames": len(self._records),
        "state_counts": {s: states.count(s) for s in STATES},
        "alert_intervals": alert,
        "warning_intervals": _intervals(times, [s == "warning" for s in states], dt),
        "danger_intervals": danger_iv,
        "actionable_intervals": _intervals(times, actionable, dt),
        "first_alert_t": first_alert,
        "first_danger_t": first_danger,
        "lead_time_s": (round(first_danger - first_alert, 4)
                        if first_alert is not None and first_danger is not None else None),
        "closest_approach": closest,
    }

    def close(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Finish all files and write the manifest; returns paths and counts.

    Returns ``{'run_dir', 'manifest', 'videos', 'stills', 'frames'}``.
    Calling it again returns the same result.
    """
    if self._result is not None:
        return self._result
    self._closed = True
    for sink in self._sinks.values():
        try:
            sink.close()
        except Exception as exc:
            _LOG.error("closing %s failed: %s", sink.path, exc)
    for fh in self._gt_files.values():
        fh.close()
    stills = self._write_stills()
    videos = {k: str(s.path.relative_to(self.run_dir)) for k, s in self._sinks.items()
              if s.frames > 0}
    frames_dir = {}
    if self.save_frames != "none":
        frames_dir = {v: f"frames/{v}" for v in self.views
                      if (self.run_dir / "frames" / v).is_dir()}
    manifest = {
        "run_id": self.run_id,
        "run": self.run.to_dict(),
        "scenario": self.scenario,
        "layout": self.layout,
        "overlay": self.overlay,
        "views": self.views,
        "cameras": self._cameras,
        "videos": videos,
        "frames_dir": frames_dir,
        "frame_ext": None if self.save_frames == "none" else self.save_frames,
        "gt": {v: f"gt/{v}.jsonl" for v in self._gt_files},
        "stills": [str(Path(p).relative_to(self.run_dir)) for p in stills],
        "timeline": self.timeline_summary(),
        "complete": self._error is None,
        "error": self._error,
        "frame_count": len(self._records),
        "frames": self._records,
    }
    path = self.run_dir / "manifest.json"
    with open(path, "w") as fh:
        json.dump(_json_safe(manifest), fh, indent=1)
    self._result = {
        "run_dir": str(self.run_dir),
        "manifest": str(path),
        "videos": [str(self.run_dir / v) for v in videos.values()],
        "stills": stills,
        "frames": len(self._records),
    }
    return self._result

    def find_ffmpeg() -> Optional[str]:
    """Path of an ffmpeg executable: the one on ``PATH``, else the ``imageio-ffmpeg`` binary."""
    exe = shutil.which("ffmpeg")
    if exe:
        return exe
    try:
        import imageio_ffmpeg

        return imageio_ffmpeg.get_ffmpeg_exe()
    except Exception:
        return None

    export ¶

    Detection datasets from a rendered run.

    A run directory written by bikeped.sim.recorder.Recorder holds the clean video of every view, optionally the individual frames, and one ground-truth file per view. The exporters here turn one view of a run into a COCO annotation file or a YOLO dataset folder with the classes person and bicycle.

    Boxes are axis-aligned and given in pixels of the exported image, with the origin at the top-left corner. Saved frames are copied as they are; when a run has no saved frames the images are decoded from the clean video of the view, whose frame k belongs to line k of the ground-truth file.

    def export_coco(
    run_dir: PathLike,
    out_path: PathLike,
    view: str = "pole",
    *,
    min_visible: float = 0.0,
    min_area: float = 0.0,
    every: int = 1,
    images_dir: Optional[PathLike] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Write one view of a run as a COCO detection dataset.

    Parameters
    ----------
    run_dir:
        Run directory with ``manifest.json`` and ``gt/<view>.jsonl``.
    out_path:
        Annotation file to write. ``bbox`` is ``[x, y, width, height]`` in
        pixels; the categories are ``person`` (id 1) and ``bicycle`` (id 2).
    view:
        Name of the camera view to export.
    min_visible:
        Drop boxes whose ``visible_fraction`` is known and below this value.
        Boxes without a visibility estimate are kept.
    min_area:
        Drop boxes smaller than this area in square pixels.
    every:
        Export every ``every``-th frame.
    images_dir:
        Folder for the images; ``images`` next to ``out_path`` by default.
        ``file_name`` in the annotation file is relative to it.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``{"images": n, "annotations": m, "path": out_path}``.
    """
    run = _load_run(run_dir, view)
    out_file = Path(out_path)
    images_root = Path(images_dir) if images_dir is not None else out_file.parent / "images"
    out_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    images_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    images: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    annotations: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for sample in _iter_samples(run, every, min_visible, min_area):
        suffix = sample.source.suffix.lower() if sample.source is not None else ".jpg"
        name = f"{run.stem}_{sample.index:06d}{suffix}"
        _store_image(sample, images_root / name)
        image_id = len(images) + 1
        images.append(
            {
                "id": image_id,
                "file_name": name,
                "width": sample.width,
                "height": sample.height,
                "frame_index": sample.index,
                "time_s": round(sample.t, 4),
            }
        )
        for box in sample.boxes:
            annotations.append(
                {
                    "id": len(annotations) + 1,
                    "image_id": image_id,
                    "category_id": box.class_index + 1,
                    "bbox": [round(v, 2) for v in (box.x, box.y, box.w, box.h)],
                    "area": round(box.w * box.h, 2),
                    "iscrowd": 0,
                    "agent_id": box.agent_id,
                    "truncation": box.truncation,
                    "visible_fraction": box.visible_fraction,
                    "distance_m": box.distance_m,
                }
            )

    info = run.manifest.get("run") or {}
    dataset = {
        "info": {
            "description": f"bikeped render {run.run_id}, view {view}",
            "version": "1.0",
            "run_id": run.run_id,
            "view": view,
            "scenario": info.get("scenario_name", ""),
            "engine": info.get("engine", ""),
            "map": info.get("map", ""),
            "weather": info.get("weather", ""),
        },
        "licenses": [],
        "images": images,
        "annotations": annotations,
        "categories": [
            {"id": i + 1, "name": name, "supercategory": _SUPERCATEGORIES[i]}
            for i, name in enumerate(CLASS_NAMES)
        ],
    }
    with open(out_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(dataset, fh)
        fh.write("\n")
    return {"images": len(images), "annotations": len(annotations), "path": str(out_file)}

Frames without boxes get an empty label file, so they count as negatives.

    def export_yolo(
    run_dir: PathLike,
    out_dir: PathLike,
    view: str = "pole",
    *,
    min_visible: float = 0.0,
    min_area: float = 0.0,
    every: int = 1,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Write one view of a run as a YOLO detection dataset.

    The output folder gets ``images/<run_id>_<view>_<frame>.jpg``, a label
    file with the same stem under ``labels/`` and a ``data.yaml``. Each label
    line is ``class cx cy w h`` with the box centre and size divided by the
    image width and height; class 0 is ``person`` and class 1 is ``bicycle``.
    Frames without boxes get an empty label file, so they count as negatives.

    ``min_visible``, ``min_area`` and ``every`` filter as in
    :func:`export_coco`. Exports of several runs into the same folder add up,
    because the file names carry the run id.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``{"images": n, "labels": m, "path": out_dir}``, where ``m`` counts
        the boxes written.
    """
    run = _load_run(run_dir, view)
    root = Path(out_dir)
    images_root = root / "images"
    labels_root = root / "labels"
    images_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    labels_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    n_images = 0
    n_labels = 0
    for sample in _iter_samples(run, every, min_visible, min_area):
        stem = f"{run.stem}_{sample.index:06d}"
        _store_image(sample, images_root / f"{stem}.jpg")
        lines = [
            "{:d} {:.6f} {:.6f} {:.6f} {:.6f}".format(
                box.class_index,
                (box.x + box.w / 2.0) / sample.width,
                (box.y + box.h / 2.0) / sample.height,
                box.w / sample.width,
                box.h / sample.height,
            )
            for box in sample.boxes
        ]
        with open(labels_root / f"{stem}.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write("".join(line + "\n" for line in lines))
        n_images += 1
        n_labels += len(lines)

    data = {
        "path": str(root.resolve()),
        "train": "images",
        "val": "images",
        "names": dict(enumerate(CLASS_NAMES)),
    }
    with open(root / "data.yaml", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        yaml.safe_dump(data, fh, sort_keys=False)
    return {"images": n_images, "labels": n_labels, "path": str(root)}
